title: Black Holes Explained: What Falls In and What Comes Out
audience: Curious adults anywhere in the world with no physics background who love big ideas explained simply.
brief: Explain what black holes are, how they form, and what the famous glowing-ring photo shows, using everyday analogies and no maths. Warm, encouraging tone that never talks down. Goal: viewers subscribe and watch the follow-up on neutron stars.

issues.description: Claims the Sun will collapse into a black hole when it dies. In fact the Sun, at about one solar mass, is far below the roughly twenty-solar-mass threshold for black hole formation; it will shed its layers and end as a white dwarf. Correct fate: white dwarf, not black hole.

Claims physicists have proven that information escapes through tiny wormholes and the paradox is fully solved. In fact the black hole information paradox is unresolved; wormhole-escape ideas are unproven hypotheses. Correct position: open problem, not settled proof.
Unexplained specialist terms (Schwarzschild radius, Eddington luminosity, magnetorotational instability) with no gloss for a no-physics-background audience.
Explains the same trampoline-and-bowling-ball gravity analogy three times in a row in slightly different words, stalling the video.
A roughly forty-second ranking of science-fiction films has nothing to do with explaining black holes and stalls the explainer.
The middle of the video promises a clear explanation of what the orange ring in the famous photo actually is, but the ending never explains it. The promise is never paid off.
Condescending lines (even a child could follow this; if you are lost, that is on you) clash with the brief's warm, encouraging, never-talk-down tone.
